# FloatLayout

The shape of one binary interchange format: where its fields are and what they mean.

```rux
pub struct FloatLayout {
    pub precision: uint;
    // private fields
}
```

## Fields

| Name        | Type   | Description                                                                      |
| ----------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `precision` | `uint` | The significand precision, counting the leading bit whether or not it is stored. |

## Methods

<h3 id="significand-field-bits"><code>SignificandFieldBits</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SignificandFieldBits(self: &FloatLayout) -> uint
```

How many bits the stored significand field has: the precision, less the leading bit unless it is written.

**Returns**: how many bits the stored significand field occupies

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloat.rux#L60)

<h3 id="minimum-exponent"><code>MinimumExponent</code></h3>

```rux
pub func MinimumExponent(self: &FloatLayout) -> int
```

The smallest exponent a normal value has, as the power of two its integer significand is scaled by.

**Returns**: the smallest exponent a normal value can have

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloat.rux#L67)

<h3 id="maximum-exponent"><code>MaximumExponent</code></h3>

```rux
pub func MaximumExponent(self: &FloatLayout) -> int
```

The largest exponent a finite value has, on the same scale.

**Returns**: the largest exponent a finite value can have

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloat.rux#L74)

<h3 id="decimal-digits"><code>DecimalDigits</code></h3>

```rux
pub func DecimalDigits(self: &FloatLayout) -> uint
```

How many decimal digits the shortest exact rendering can need: one more than the precision is worth.

**Returns**: how many decimal digits round-trip through this format

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloat.rux#L81)

## Related

<h3 id="wide-class"><code>WideClass</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum WideClass: int32 {
    Zero = 0,
    Subnormal = 1,
    Normal = 2,
    Infinity = 3,
    NaN = 4
}
```

What kind of value a bit pattern holds.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloat.rux#L88)

**Cases**

| Name        | Value | Description                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Zero`      | `0`   | Zero of either sign.                                                              |
| `Subnormal` | `1`   | A value below the normal range, with no leading bit.                              |
| `Normal`    | `2`   | An ordinary finite value.                                                         |
| `Infinity`  | `3`   | Infinity of either sign.                                                          |
| `NaN`       | `4`   | Not a number, including the unnormal and pseudo encodings of the extended format. |

<h3 id="pack-wide"><code>PackWide</code></h3>

    negative: bool,

Puts a finite value back together under `layout`, which must already be within range and precision.

**Returns**: the bit pattern for that sign, significand and exponent
